final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally correct: prior approval and the informal monitoring note are only contextual, aggregate readiness alone is insufficient, and any defensible certification theory would have to rely on current-release documentation and explicit disclosure of the field-service dispatch weakness. But that caveat is not merely a disclosure note attached to an otherwise complete certification. It is an unresolved compliance predicate required by policy. The admissible evidence shows aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also shows a current named-use-case subgroup regression and no evidence that the required current-release documentation or approved mitigation already exists. Because the missing predicate remains unresolved, the supportable conclusion stays suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation has been updated to reflect current evaluation results for this release.
No admissible evidence shows the field-service dispatch limitation is explicitly disclosed in the current release documentation.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or formal risk acceptance covering the subgroup regression before launch.
The policy predicate for certification is still unmet on the present record, so the record supports at most a possible path to compliance, not completed compliance today.
